A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research and contain readable main text, equations, all 17 figures, and Appendices A-I. Text extraction and rendered-page comparisons support a reliable, complete comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original integer least-squares and compressed-sensing experiments. Appendices C, H, and I report additional reduction, runtime, and algorithm-variant experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical results in Section 5 and Appendices C, H, and I, including performance, runtime, and iteration measurements.

M1.justification: The DS decompositions, continuous reformulation, DCA-LS in Algorithm 1, and DCA-Restart in Appendix I are unchanged. The revised Appendix C bound does not change either procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic integer least-squares and compressed-sensing tasks and Appendix C's submodular quadratic problem. The domains and noise, sparsity, and discretization scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding least-squares comparisons retain ADMM, RAR, OBQ, and Gurobi's optimal solution where used; compressed sensing retains LASSO and OMP. Appendix I retains the same DCA-Restart comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix G retain the same data generation, dimensions, noise levels, metrics, initialization, parameter grids, and iteration limits. The evaluation protocols in Appendices C, H, and I also match.

E4.justification: Appendix C's reduction-cost study, Appendix H's sensitivity and runtime analyses, and Appendix I's initialization, variant, and iteration comparisons are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report 100-run averages and standard-deviation error bars for the main and DCA-variant experiments, and 50 trials for Appendix C. No repeated-run or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All empirical plots in Figures 1-17 are visually identical, and the associated numerical and qualitative findings are unchanged. No performance, runtime, or iteration results are added, removed, or corrected.

T1.justification: Appendix C changes the reduced function's Lipschitz upper bound from (k - 1) sqrt((k - 1)n) max_i B_i to (2k - 3) sqrt((k - 1)n) max_i B_i, updating the stated multiplier accordingly. This is a localized mathematical correction; the asymptotic complexity discussion and other propositions and proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same claims about DS representability, the continuous reformulation, DCA-LS convergence to a local minimum, and empirical advantages on the two applications.

C2.justification: The explanations of reduction overhead, initialization dependence, runtime tradeoffs, and limitations of continuous-domain guarantees remain unchanged. The revised Appendix C coefficient does not alter its qualitative interpretation.

D1.justification: The code-access information and Appendix G's MATLAB implementations, solver details, stopping criteria, initialization instructions, and parameter settings are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 3.2 adds Chen et al. (2017), Strong NP-hardness for sparse optimization with concave penalty functions, to support the existing sparse-optimization hardness statement. The broader research positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 5.1 rearranges and lightly rewrites its opening paragraph, introducing the ILS abbreviation and placing the optimization formulation before the application examples. The correspondence email and arXiv version text also change; section and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: The added reference causes limited bibliography reflow across pages 10-12, including moving the Pham Dinh and Le Thi entry onto page 12. All figures, captions, and algorithm displays retain their layout.

improvement.justification: Replacing k - 1 with 2k - 3 in Appendix C repairs a localized Lipschitz-bound error, while the added Chen et al. citation supplies attribution for an existing hardness statement. These improve mathematical accuracy and sourcing modestly; the algorithms, main guarantees, and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
